angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 56,546,746 km at 13302.65 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 0.0752 +/- 0.0112 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 13302.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 81.280 (74.451 to 85.542) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 56,546,746 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 7.393 (7.353 to 7.596) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5133 +/- 44.3 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 428584689010934016: teff_gspphot 5132.698 K (16th-84th percentiles 5054.3105-5142.9707), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 428584689010934016: teff_gspphot 5132.698 K (16th-84th percentiles 5054.3105-5142.9707), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gaia-dr3-428584689010934016.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 1.487, rounded to two decimals
